headline_en: BSF returns two Bangladeshis who entered India
summary_en: India's Border Security Force (BSF) handed back two Bangladeshi men detained for illegally entering India's Assam state across the Nageshwari border in Kurigram. They were returned at a BGB-BSF flag meeting on the zero line on Monday night (13 April 2026) and passed to Kachakata police station. Their families say they crossed by mistake in bad weather.

facts.statement: On Sunday night (about 12 April 2026) two Bangladeshi men crossed from the North Jhaukuti (Uttar Jhaukuti) border, Choddoghori area, Narayanpur union, Nageshwari upazila, Kurigram, into Takimari area of Dhubri district, Assam state, India; local people there detained them and handed them to India's BSF.

On Monday night (13 April 2026) BSF returned the two detained Bangladeshis to Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) through a BGB-BSF flag meeting held on the zero line of the Nageshwari border, Kurigram; BGB then handed them to Kachakata police station, with family members present.

In the Nageshwari (Kurigram) case of April 2026, the families of the two men informed the Choddoghori BOP (border outpost); BGB then wrote a letter to BSF, and a flag meeting between the two forces was held the next afternoon, after which BSF handed the men to BGB.
The officer-in-charge of Kachakata police station, Arpan Kumar Das, said in April 2026 that the two Bangladeshis returned by BSF would be handed to their families after the necessary legal process.
facts.source_in_article: Arpan Kumar Das, OC, Kachakata police station

facts.statement: The families of the two men returned from India in April 2026 claimed they crossed the border after losing their way in bad weather.

headline_en: Mother Hosne Ara wants to see her son's face one last time
summary_en: Mehedi Hasan (21) from Feni, who went to Iraq five months earlier with his father's help, died on Wednesday (about 4 March 2026) along with two other Bangladeshis; the family says from poisoning in iftar food. The family borrowed about 10 lakh taka to send him and wants government help to bring the body home. Feni Sadar UNO said the administration had not been formally informed.

facts.statement: Mehedi Hasan (21) of Debipur village, Sharshadi union, Feni Sadar, died in Iraq on Wednesday (about 4 March 2026); his family claims it was from food poisoning from iftar food, and the Bangladesh Embassy in Baghdad also reported the death in a condolence message.

In Iraq, Mehedi Hasan and two others ate iftar together on Tuesday (about 3 March 2026), fell ill, were taken to a local hospital, got first aid and returned home that night; they ate sehri and went to sleep, and colleagues found all three dead in their room the next afternoon. The other two dead were Mohammad Tarek (45) of Brahmanbaria and his son Md. Sabbir (22).

Mehedi Hasan's family borrowed about 10 lakh taka to send him to Iraq through his father, who has worked in Iraq's Kurdistan region for about eight years; Mehedi went in October of the previous year (2025).
Mehedi Hasan's mother Hosne Ara asked for government help to bring his body home from Iraq in March 2026.

Feni Sadar UNO Sultana Nasrin said in March 2026 that the administration had not been formally told of the death in Iraq and no one from the family had informed them; once informed, necessary help would be given after discussion with the district administration.

summary_en: Nurul Alam (38) of Akbarpara, Adhunagar union, Lohagara, Chattogram, who had lived in Saudi Arabia for 18 years and ran a cloth business in Mahail, Abha, Asir province, was killed when his microbus collided with a cargo lorry on Thursday night (about 4 December 2025). His father is gathering papers to bring the body home; the union parishad chairman says the union and upazila administration are helping.

facts.statement: Nurul Alam (38) of Akbarpara village, Adhunagar union, Lohagara upazila, Chattogram, was killed on the spot in Saudi Arabia on Thursday (about 4 December 2025) at about 10:30 pm Bangladesh time when the microbus he was driving home after deliveries collided with a cargo lorry.

Nurul Alam went to Saudi Arabia 18 years before (about 2007) right after passing SSC; he first learnt tailoring, worked about 10 years at a firm, then eight years ago started his own cloth business in Mahail area, Abha city, Asir province, delivering cloth to shops in his own microbus.

Nurul Alam took his younger brother Nurunnabi to Saudi Arabia 10 years ago, and about 11 days before his death arranged for his mother and aunt to go to Saudi Arabia for Umrah; they were still there when he died.
In December 2025 Nurul Alam's father Saleh Ahmad (68) was rushing to send the necessary papers to bring his son's body home from Saudi Arabia; when the body would arrive was still unknown.

Adhunagar union parishad chairman Nazim Uddin said in December 2025 that the union parishad and upazila administration were giving all necessary help to bring Nurul Alam's body home from Saudi Arabia.

headline_en: Bangladesh Bank makes buying air tickets for foreign travel easier
summary_en: Bangladesh Bank issued a directive on Wednesday 19 November 2025 letting Bangladeshi citizens buy any international air ticket themselves, from home, with any internationally usable card, without going to an agency or bank. The previous USD 300 per-transaction limit on foreign-currency card payments no longer applies to air tickets; tickets can be bought within the card's foreign-currency limit and the amount can be refilled.

facts.statement: Under a Bangladesh Bank directive issued on Wednesday 19 November 2025, Bangladeshi citizens can buy any air ticket to an international destination themselves from home with any card used for international transactions, without going to any agency or bank.

Before the 19 November 2025 Bangladesh Bank directive, card users could not buy any good or service costing more than USD 300 in foreign currency in one go; that limit has been lifted for air tickets, which can now be bought at any price within the credit card's foreign-currency limit.

Bangladesh Bank said (November 2025) that after buying an air ticket on an international card, the same amount can be refilled to the card, provided the ticket payment was made entirely through a bank in Bangladesh; banks must keep a separate record of the ticket purchase for each refill.

The November 2025 Bangladesh Bank circular says foreign airlines must deposit ticket-sale income in their foreign-currency accounts with authorised dealer banks in Bangladesh, while locally owned airlines must convert collected money into taka before depositing.

Industry people said in November 2025 that the new Bangladesh Bank rule will let travellers buy tickets easily, ensure competitive prices, reduce the gap between local and foreign ticket prices, and reduce middlemen's influence on tickets to foreign destinations.

headline_en: Why Bangladeshi students choose Australia for higher education
summary_en: A feature on why Australia is popular with Bangladeshi students: universities in Canberra, Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth, part-time work up to 20 hours a week, post-study work visas of two to four years, and several named scholarships.

facts.statement: According to a Prothom Alo feature (October 2025), students in Australia can work up to 20 hours a week alongside study.
According to the October 2025 feature, after finishing study in Australia a work visa of two to four years can be obtained, which opens a path to permanent residence.
Melbourne International Undergraduate Scholarship: up to 10,000 dollars tuition fee waiver for the first year for undergraduate students (as described in an October 2025 Prothom Alo feature).

Monash International Leadership Scholarship: 100 percent financial support up to a set number of credit points for undergraduate and postgraduate students (as described in an October 2025 Prothom Alo feature).

UTS Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship: the university covers up to 50 percent of study costs for undergraduate and postgraduate students (as described in an October 2025 Prothom Alo feature).

Global Academic Excellence Scholarship: 50 percent reduction in study costs for outstanding performers in each faculty (as described in an October 2025 Prothom Alo feature; the university is not named).
The October 2025 feature names Canberra, Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth as Australian cities with top universities, and says many students go from Bangladesh every year.

headline_en: Documents needed to go abroad for higher education
summary_en: A general checklist of 11 documents needed to study abroad: passport, offer letter, academic certificates and transcripts, language test scores, proof of funds, medical report, visa form and fee, photos, recommendation letters, statement of purpose and letter of motivation. It warns that a wrong or incomplete document can get an application rejected.

facts.statement: A Prothom Alo guide (October 2025) says a student going abroad needs a valid passport that stays valid at least for the length of study, and should renew it before it expires.
The October 2025 guide says the offer letter (admission confirmation from the university applied to) is very important during the student visa process.
The October 2025 guide says students must submit SSC, HSC, bachelor's or master's certificates and mark sheets, officially translated and attested, especially if not in English.
The October 2025 guide says most foreign universities require proof of English such as IELTS, GRE, GMAT, SAT or TOEFL scores, with required scores varying by country and university.
The October 2025 guide says students must prove they can pay tuition and living costs with a bank statement or sponsorship letter; some countries require a set amount shown as a bank deposit.
The October 2025 guide says many countries require a medical report or health certificate for students, and it is especially important for Australia, Canada and New Zealand.

The October 2025 guide warns that wrong information on the visa application form is one of the main reasons for visa delay or refusal, and that any wrong or incomplete document can get the application cancelled.
The October 2025 guide says passport-size photos must follow each country's size, background and format rules, and photo studios will usually take photos to the right size if told the country.
The October 2025 guide says universities usually want two to three recommendation letters from teachers or workplace supervisors, plus a statement of purpose and a letter of motivation.

headline_en: BSF sends back 31 Bangladeshis through Darshana border, Chuadanga
summary_en: On 25 October 2025 India's BSF handed 31 Bangladeshis to BGB at a flag meeting at the Darshana Joynagar-Gede point, Chuadanga. Most had entered India illegally at different times and were living and working as labourers in Haryana state, where Haryana police detained them. They were passed to Darshana police for verification and return to families.

facts.statement: On Saturday 25 October 2025 at midday, India's BSF handed 31 Bangladeshis (16 men, 10 women, two third-gender people and three children) to BGB through a flag meeting on the zero line at Darshana Joynagar (Chuadanga) and Gede (India) point; BGB Darshana company commander Md. Abu Hasan and BSF Gede company commander Shiv Shankar Singh led the meeting.

According to Lt Col Mohammad Nazmul Hasan, commander of the Chuadanga battalion (6 BGB), the 31 Bangladeshis returned on 25 October 2025 had entered India illegally at different times; most were living and working as labourers in Haryana state, and Haryana police detained them and handed them to BSF.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Col Mohammad Nazmul Hasan, 6 BGB

facts.statement: The 31 Bangladeshis returned from India via Darshana on 25 October 2025 came from Chuadanga, Narail, Noakhali, Kurigram, Dhaka, Khulna, Satkhira, Cumilla, Mymensingh, Feni, Gopalganj, Moulvibazar, Sherpur and Manikganj.

After the 25 October 2025 return, BGB handed the 31 to Darshana police, who would verify addresses and details; Darshana OC Muhammad Shahid Titumir said they would be kept at Parkrishnapur-Madna union parishad, families informed, and taken home with help from police in their home areas.

headline_en: Expatriates in Portugal in trouble over residence permits
summary_en: Portugal's immigration agency AIMA is demanding a declaration from the original house owner as proof of residence, and detailed proof of income scaled to family size, for residence card renewals, leaving Bangladeshis and other migrants unable to renew. A new immigration law tightening family reunification was approved by parliament on 30 September 2025 and takes effect after presidential approval.

facts.statement: In 2025 Portugal's immigration agency AIMA imposed tough conditions for residence permit renewal: proof of residence in the form of a declaration from the original house owner, and detailed proof of income (income declaration, scaled to the number of family members if the family is large).
Migrants in Portugal had for a long time been unable to renew residence cards; in June 2025 AIMA opened an opportunity for renewal, but still demanded a landlord's declaration as proof of residence.
On 30 September 2025 Portugal's parliament approved a new immigration law that tightens family reunification conditions and other matters; it will take effect only after the President's approval.

Bangladeshi expatriate Kamruzzaman, about six years in Portugal, said he had always got and renewed his residence card using an address certificate from the local municipality, but under the new rule his landlord will not give the required certificate, leaving his status uncertain.
Prothom Alo's Dur Porobash section accepts readers' stories from abroad at email dp@prothomalo.com.

headline_en: Bangladeshi wins lottery worth Tk 66.34 crore in Abu Dhabi
summary_en: Harun Sardar Nur Nabi Sardar (44), a Bangladeshi taxi driver in Sharjah living in the UAE since 2009, won the Big Ticket Abu Dhabi first prize of 20 million dirhams (about Tk 66.34 crore) announced on 3 October 2025, shared among 11 people. Other Bangladeshis won smaller prizes.

facts.statement: Harun Sardar Nur Nabi Sardar (44), a Bangladeshi taxi driver living in Sharjah, UAE, since 2009 whose family lives in Bangladesh, won the 'Big Ticket Abu Dhabi' first prize of 2 crore (20 million) dirhams, about Tk 66.34 crore, announced on Friday 3 October 2025; he bought the ticket on 14 September for a group of 11 people who will share the prize, and he buys a Big Ticket every month.

In the same Big Ticket draw (3 October 2025), Bangladeshi Ali Hussain Ali was one of four winners of 50,000 dirhams (about Tk 16.58 lakh); Bangladeshi Jajrul Islam Fakir Ahmed of Al Ain won 150,000 dirhams (Tk 49.75 lakh) in 'Spin the Wheel', to share with 10 people; and Mohammad Saiful Islam Ahmed Nabi of Sharjah won a Range Rover Velar car.

people_cases.what_happened: Won Big Ticket Abu Dhabi first prize of 20 million dirhams with 10 others

headline_en: Returnee migrant Lokman succeeds in off-season watermelon farming
summary_en: Lokman Hossain (30) of Charwadel, Chandradwip union, Bauphal, Patuakhali, went abroad in 2018 after graduating and came home in early 2022 because the work was very hard. He now grows off-season hybrid watermelon with mulching on 5 decimals, earning about one lakh taka from a Tk 20,000 outlay; the upazila agriculture officer promised support.

facts.statement: Lokman Hossain (30) of Charwadel village, Chandradwip union, Bauphal, Patuakhali, went abroad for work in 2018 after graduating and returned in early 2022, saying he had to do very hard physical work abroad; he then started farming with his father. The destination country is not named.

Returnee Lokman Hossain says he spent only Tk 20,000 on a previous off-season watermelon crop on 5 decimals of land and sold about one lakh taka worth, and expects about one lakh taka profit in 2025 from the same 5 decimals, using hybrid watermelon with mulching in the rainy season.
Bauphal upazila agriculture officer Md. Milon said in September 2025 that the agriculture department would give returnee farmer Lokman Hossain all kinds of support for off-season watermelon farming.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Milon, Bauphal upazila agriculture officer

headline_en: Six detained while crossing into India through Chunarughat border; brokers flee
summary_en: BGB's 55 battalion detained six men from Boail village, Khaliajuri, Netrokona, before dawn on Sunday 21 September 2025 near border pillar 1961/7-S in Chunarughat, Habiganj, as they tried to cross into India through a broker ring for Durga Puja. They had paid brokers Tk 10,000 each; the brokers fled. A case was filed against the six for attempted illegal crossing.

facts.statement: Before dawn on Sunday 21 September 2025, six men from Boail village, Khaliajuri upazila, Netrokona, tried to cross into India near border pillar 1961/7-S in Chunarughat upazila, Habiganj, through a broker ring, and were detained by a 55 BGB patrol.

The six men detained at the Chunarughat border on 21 September 2025 said they each paid Tk 10,000 to a broker ring to be taken across the border into India, to go there for Durga Puja; the brokers fled when BGB caught them.

According to the detainees, as told by 55 BGB commander Lt Col Tanzilur Rahman, Toufiq, Milon and Hakim, members of a human trafficking ring from the Jamburachhara area of Sreemangal, lured them with the promise of reaching India for Tk 10,000 per person.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Col Tanzilur Rahman, 55 BGB battalion, Habiganj

facts.statement: The six detained at the Chunarughat border on 21 September 2025 were handed to Chunarughat police station that afternoon and a case was filed against them for attempting to cross the border illegally.

headline_en: Claim of 'Graduate Pass' for 10,000 Bangladeshi students is false: Malaysia's higher education minister
summary_en: Malaysia's Higher Education Minister Zambry Abd Kadir said in a statement on 23 August 2025 that reports of a 'Graduate Pass' giving 10,000 Bangladeshi students in Malaysia work opportunities are false, and that no such agreement was made during Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus's visit to Malaysia. He rebuked Kedah state committee chairman Haim Hilman Abdullah, who had claimed this in a TikTok video.

facts.statement: On Saturday 23 August 2025 Malaysia's Higher Education Minister Zambry Abd Kadir said in a statement (reported by The Star) that the spreading report that 10,000 Bangladeshi students studying in Malaysia would be given a 'Graduate Pass' to work is untrue and baseless, and that Malaysia has given no consent to this.
facts.source_in_article: Zambry Abd Kadir, Malaysia Higher Education Minister, via The Star

facts.statement: Malaysia's Higher Education Minister said in August 2025 that no agreement was signed during Bangladesh Chief Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus's recent visit to Malaysia that would oblige Malaysia to give work opportunities to 10,000 Bangladeshi students.

The claim that 10,000 Bangladeshi students would get jobs in Malaysia came from a 2 minute 19 second TikTok video by Haim Hilman Abdullah, chairman of Kedah state's committee on industry and investment, higher education, science, technology and innovation, based on a Bangladeshi newspaper report; Malaysia's minister called it entirely false and irresponsible.

headline_en: Bangladeshi youth dies while learning to drive in Saudi Arabia
summary_en: Sakibur Rahman (25) of Mohuripara, Pekua, Cox's Bazar, who went to Saudi Arabia on 6 June 2025, was killed in a road accident in Mahil (Mahail) city on 23 July 2025 at about 7 pm Bangladesh time while learning to drive. A relative was injured. Papers are being collected to bring the body home.

facts.statement: Sakibur Rahman (25) of Mohuripara, Pekua upazila, Cox's Bazar, who went to Saudi Arabia on 6 June 2025, died on the spot in a road accident in Mahil city, Saudi Arabia, on Wednesday 23 July 2025 at about 7 pm Bangladesh time while learning to drive; another relative was injured.
Magnama union parishad panel chairman Badiul Alam said in July 2025 that papers were being collected to bring Sakibur Rahman's body home from Saudi Arabia.
facts.source_in_article: Badiul Alam, panel chairman, Magnama UP

headline_en: Eid gathering and data-collection workshop of Khulna expatriates in the UAE
summary_en: NRB Khulna, an association of expatriates from Khulna, held an Eid gathering and data-collection workshop at Hudaibiya Hall, Sharjah, on 12 July 2025 to record the skills and professional profiles of expatriate professionals. It followed a request to the Bangladesh Consul General in Dubai and Northern Emirates for a skills-based database of expatriate professionals.

facts.statement: On Saturday evening 12 July 2025 NRB Khulna, an organisation of Khulna expatriates (coordinator engineer Moinul Islam), held an Eid gathering and data-collection workshop at Hudaibiya Hall, Sharjah, UAE, to collect and store skills, experience and professional profiles of expatriate professionals.

Greater Khulna expatriates had earlier asked the Bangladesh Consul General and consular officials in Dubai and Northern Emirates, at a meeting, to create a detailed skills-based database of expatriate professionals; the July 2025 workshop continued that effort.
Prothom Alo's Dur Porobash section accepts readers' stories from abroad at email dp@prothomalo.com.

headline_en: Rakib, who revived closed factories, dies in boat accident in Canada
BGB brings back 24 Bangladeshis detained after going to India for work
summary_en: BGB brought back 24 Bangladeshis (8 men, 8 women, 8 children) detained by India's BSF at the Phulbari border, Kurigram, after a flag meeting near pillar 932 at Balatari at about 1:30 am on 24 May 2025. They had gone to Delhi for work and were caught by BSF while returning home; they were handed to their families.

facts.statement: At about 1:30 am after Friday 23 May 2025, BGB brought back 24 Bangladeshis (8 men, 8 women and 8 children) detained by BSF, after a flag meeting beside border pillar 932 at Balatari border, Phulbari upazila, Kurigram; BSF's 03 battalion AC SHL Simti and Lalmonirhat 15 BGB deputy commander Major Hasnain led the meeting.

The 24 Bangladeshis returned at Phulbari, Kurigram, in May 2025 had gone to Delhi, India, looking for work, and were detained by BSF while coming back to Bangladesh; how long before they had gone could not be confirmed.

After the hour-long flag meeting in May 2025, BGB formally handed the 24 returnees from India directly to their families with help from local people and public representatives (Naodanga UP chairman Hasen Ali was present).

headline_en: Saudi expatriate due home on leave dies when vehicle overturns on shopping trip for relatives
summary_en: Saiful Islam (28) of East Belagaon, Jayfarnagar union, Juri, Moulvibazar, a poultry-farm worker near Riyadh for about three years, was killed on 20 May 2025 when the goods truck he rode to Riyadh to shop hit a camel on the road and overturned. His employer had given him three months' leave and he was due home on 5 June. His body is at a Riyadh hospital morgue.

facts.statement: On Tuesday 20 May 2025 at about 4 pm Saudi time, Saiful Islam (28) of East Belagaon, Jayfarnagar union, Juri upazila, Moulvibazar, was killed on the spot near Riyadh when the goods-carrying truck he and co-worker Bablu Mia were riding to Riyadh city on their weekly day off hit a camel standing on the road and overturned; Bablu and the Pakistani driver were injured, and police rescued them.

Saiful Islam worked about three years as a labourer on a poultry farm in a village near Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, without coming home; his employer recently gave him three months' leave and he was due home on 5 June 2025.
After the 20 May 2025 accident, Saiful Islam's body was kept at a hospital morgue in Riyadh, and injured co-worker Bablu Mia (of West Belagaon) was admitted to a local hospital.

headline_en: Saudi expatriate electrocuted a week before his wedding
summary_en: Juned Ahmad (28) of West Kachurgul, Goalbari union, Juri, Moulvibazar, who had gone to Saudi Arabia about a year earlier as an electrician after learning electrical repair, was electrocuted at home on 15 May 2025 while connecting a neighbour's new refrigerator, during home leave a week before his wedding. Police sent the body for post-mortem.

facts.statement: Juned Ahmad (28) of West Kachurgul, Goalbari union, Juri, Moulvibazar, learned electrical repair work after passing HSC and went to Saudi Arabia about a year before May 2025, where he worked as an electrician; he came home on leave 10-15 days before his death.

On Thursday evening 15 May 2025, Saudi expatriate Juned Ahmad, home on leave, was electrocuted while connecting a newly bought refrigerator at neighbour Abdur Nur's house in the same village and died on the way to the upazila health complex; Juri OC Md. Murshedul Alam Bhuiyan said the body was sent to the 250-bed hospital morgue in Moulvibazar for post-mortem.
facts.source_in_article: police and local sources; OC Md. Murshedul Alam Bhuiyan
